QF.id: AIF Valuation Taxation and Good Practices_33

question.text: Withholding tax for non-resident investors is deducted:

answer.text: By the Investment Fund at the time of credit or payment, whichever is earlier, at rates in force or applicable DTAA rates

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the AIF (Category I and II) Distributors workbook (p. 255), Section 194LBB requires the Investment Fund to withhold tax on non-business income payable to non-resident investors at the rates in force or the applicable Double Taxation Avoidance Agreement (DTAA) rate, at the time of credit of such income to the account of the payee or at the time of payment, whichever is earlier. The Trap: Withholding is not linked to the non-resident's physical visit to India, nor is it deferred to the end of the fund tenure. Non-resident investors are not exempt from withholding on Investment Fund distributions of non-business income. Note: The trigger is the earlier of credit or payment, and the rate is the rate in force or the applicable DTAA rate, as stated on p. 255 of the source.
